videos.title: History of Milk — The Drink Most Humans Can't Drink
videos.description:
Seventy percent of people on Earth can't drink milk. That's not a disease. That's the default. You're the exception.
This is the story of how one random genetic mutation ten thousand years ago set off a chain of events that ended in a nine-hundred-billion-dollar industry, sacred cows protected by law, children dying from a glass of milk bought at a market stall, and a five-dollar oat latte in a paper cup.
Milk is not just a drink. It's war, religion, politics, and one of the most powerful lobbying tools in the history of the food industry. And most people on the planet have no idea any of these stories exist.

videos.title: The History of 7UP — The Drink Without a Single Owner
videos.description:
The History of 7UP — The Drink Without a Single Owner

7UP has one of the strangest stories in soft drink history. Its original formula contained lithium, its name remains a mystery, and today the brand is split between two competing corporations: Keurig Dr Pepper in the United States and PepsiCo in international markets.

This documentary explores the history of 7UP — from its creation in 1929 and the controversial lithium formula to the famous “Uncola” campaign, its acquisition by Philip Morris, and the corporate split that still exists today.

videos.title: THE HISTORY OF KINDER — The Chocolate Egg That's Illegal in the US
videos.description:
A tiny chocolate egg with a toy inside. Banned by US federal law since before it even existed. Smuggled across borders for decades. Made by a man nobody has ever seen a real photo of.

This is the story of Kinder — from a broke candy maker in post-war Italy to a $20 billion empire that couldn't legally sell its most famous product in America for almost 80 years.

videos.title: The History of Champagne — From Accident to Luxury
videos.description:
What do a monk who hated bubbles, Napoleon, the Nazi occupation of France, and a bottle of Champagne on your holiday table have in common?
As it turns out, they all helped shape Champagne into what it is today.
In this video, we're diving into the complete history of Champagne—from a winemaking accident that caused bottles to explode underground to the drink that became the ultimate symbol of luxury, celebration, and victory.
You'll discover why Dom Pérignon didn't actually invent Champagne, how the English played a crucial role in creating modern sparkling wine, why Louis XIV turned it into a symbol of power, how Veuve Clicquot changed the entire industry, why thousands of bottles were hidden in underground tunnels during World War II, and why France is still fighting legal battles around the world over the right to use the name "Champagne."
Every bottle tells a story that has been centuries in the making.

videos.title: The History of Mentos — They Made a Soda Fountain and Became Famous for Free
videos.description:
Two street performers built a soda fountain out of mints and diet cola in 2006. The company had nothing to do with it — didn't pay a cent, didn't even know it was happening. It became one of the biggest early viral videos on the internet. And somehow it also sparked a nationwide rumor that eating the candy with soda could kill you.

videos.title: The History of Vodka — The Drink Governments Used to Control People for 500 Years
videos.description:
Most people think vodka is just a drink.

But somehow, this clear liquid has started wars, built cities, funded empires, inspired countless myths, and even sparked international battles over who can claim to have invented it.

Some of the most famous stories you've heard about vodka are completely false. Others are so unbelievable that they sound made up—even though they're true.

And perhaps the strangest part is that, after 500 years, vodka may still be doing exactly what it was always meant to do.

So... how did we get here?

videos.title: The History of Cigarettes — Deadliest Product Ever Sold
videos.description:
The History of Cigarettes — Deadliest Product Ever Sold

Tobacco kills more than 8 million people every year. Over the last century, smoking has taken more lives than both World Wars combined. And yet billions of people still buy the very thing that's killing them, every single day.

This is the story of how a sacred plant used by Indigenous peoples of Central America became a global industry built on fifty years of scientific deception. Royal bans and executions for smoking. An inventor who was refused the $75,000 prize he'd been promised. An advertising campaign that turned cigarettes into a symbol of women's freedom. Tobacco companies that knew about cancer decades before they ever admitted it publicly. And lawsuits that cost the industry hundreds of billions of dollars.

In this video: the complete history of cigarettes, from Mayan religious rituals to the modern vaping industry.
